round3_pm_finding_and_correction.the_pm_found_my_false_positive: I ran a new gate (evidence_contains_claim) and it reported that the BoC retail card's previous '+0.6%' was unevidenced. I acted on that and overwrote the value with a false claim that the evidence was missing, while the card's own summary and reason still said '+0.6% prior' -- the page then contradicted itself. The round-3 PM caught it: the bound FXStreet capture (sha 8fde58ae...) pins matching_row with previous = 0.6 for the 2026-09-24 Canada Retail Sales (MoM) event, so the number was evidenced all along.
round3_pm_finding_and_correction.why_the_gate_was_wrong: The numeric matcher emitted sign-derived and digit-fragment variants ('+0.6' for '+0.6%', '-6' for '0.6%'), so a real 0.6 in a capture never matched. It also could not distinguish a national figure from a provincial row: the statcan capture contains 0.6 as the NOVA SCOTIA line.
fixes: _numeric_variants rewritten to match on the numeric value only, across 0.6 / 0.60 / 0.600 / .6.
A pinned matching_row is now treated as evidence in its own right and is searched directly.
Added a scope check: a number that occurs only alongside sub-national labels, on a card that pins no matching_row, is flagged as possibly provincial.
previous restored to '+0.6%', bound to matching_row; the self-contradicting note removed.
round3_pm_finding_and_correction.lesson: A gate that cries wolf is worse than no gate. Two of my three 'fixes this round' were made on the authority of a machine check rather than a source, and one of those checks was itself wrong. The PM's independent verification is what caught it.

What changed in iteration-03/04 is traceability and honesty, not the call: the Michigan card is now bound to captures that actually contain 48.1 and the 47.6 consensus, the ZN=F window was rebuilt for the Sep 25 final release, and what_is_priced / falsifiers / attention_budget are now actually rendered. decision_brief.headline: Fed holds 3.75-4.00% into Oct 27-28; BoC holds 2.25% into Oct 28. Neither board has a priced single-meeting distribution we can verify, so there is no edge to express. The asymmetry to watch is the Canadian consumer, not the policy rate.
decision_brief.summary: This is an abstention on POSITION, not on VIEW. Both central banks are on hold with the next decisions inside five weeks, and the only pricing we can verify is contract-level: ZQV26 at 96.11 implies a 3.89% October average EFFR against a 3.75-4.00% target, and CRAU26's quote side implies roughly 2.378% average CORRA against a 2.25% policy rate. Both numbers are quarterly averages, not meeting odds, and neither licenses a probability. What the evidence does support is a directional asymmetry: the dovish side carries a 48.1 Michigan final print that BEAT consensus, while Canada's July retail sales contracted 0.7% in headline and 1.1% in volume. The consumer is weakening on both sides of the border while both boards sit still, which is a slow-burn risk to the October hold rather than a reason to front-run it.

what_is_priced.fed: ZQV26 (October 30-day Fed funds) closed 96.11 on Sep 25, implying a 3.89% October average EFFR. That is the midpoint of the current 3.75-4.00% range to within a basis point (the range maps to prices 96.00-96.25), so the market is pricing no October move in the contract's dominant period. The contract's 30-day average is set almost entirely before the Oct 28 decision, so this is NOT the market's view of the meeting.
what_is_priced.boc: CRAU26 (three-month CORRA) quote side 97.62/97.6225 implies roughly 2.378% average CORRA against a 2.25% policy rate — a small upward drift across the whole quarter, which spans both the Oct 28 and Dec 9 decisions. It cannot be decomposed into either meeting.
what_is_priced.unavailable: CME FedWatch returned HTTP 403 on a fresh request. No direct meeting distribution exists for either board in this snapshot, and none is estimated.

changes_since_previous: Michigan sentiment is now the September FINAL 48.1, published Sep 25 10:00 ET, which beat the 47.6 Reuters consensus and the 47.8 preliminary. The prior published snapshot carried the preliminary 47.8; this is a real data change, not a restatement.

Canada July retail sales is reclassified from hawkish to dovish. The -0.7% headline beat the -0.8% consensus, but a smaller-than-feared contraction is still a contraction (-1.1% in volume terms). The previous build labelled it 'beat' and put it on the hawkish side, which was a sign error.
The BoC hawkish column is now empty. With retail moved and no other hawkish card carrying weight, the Canadian rope reads dovish-biased rather than balanced.

macro_driver_recalculation is restamped to this payload's as_of (2026-09-28T19:05:00-04:00); it previously carried a Sep 27 stamp with a 23-day age count that was off by one, and the weight rule text itself still quoted the older 05:37:17 stamp.
The ZQV26 proxy now carries an explicit horizon caveat: the October contract is dominated by the pre-decision rate and is not a meeting proxy.
falsifiers: A verified single-meeting distribution showing more than a 10bp implied move — reachable only if FedWatch stops returning 403 — converts this from an abstention into a tradeable view.

ZQV26 closing outside 96.00-96.25 — the band that corresponds to the current 3.75-4.00% target range, i.e. an implied October average EFFR at or beyond either edge — breaks the 'no October move' premise the frame rests on.
Oct 2 Employment Situation materially above the path implied by the 3.875% midpoint puts December in play.
The October preliminary Michigan on Oct 9 printing above 51.0 would undercut the soft-consumer anchor this brief leans on.
Sep 29 Canada GDP by industry showing a second consecutive contraction turns consumer weakness from a signal into a trend and justifies an outright dovish stance rather than a neutral one.
largest_pnl_risks: Short-dated rates into Oct 28: with no verifiable meeting distribution, any position sized off the ZQV26 3.89% implied average is sized off a quarterly contract, not an October decision. The contract can move on December repricing without the Fed moving.
Oct 2 NFP is the first hard-activity print in the window and lands six business days before the FOMC. A beat there is the cheapest way to get hurt on a short-vol front-end position sized for a hold.
The BoC hawkish column being empty means the Canadian rope reads dovish purely by absence. If retail is revised up, the dovish lean disappears without any new data arriving.
Both boards' next decisions fall inside five weeks, so the 'no edge' call has a natural expiry: by the second week of October the absence of pricing data becomes a view on the data itself.
decision_brief.attention_budget: If you have 90 seconds: the Fed is on hold at 3.75-4.00% into Oct 27-28, the BoC is on hold at 2.25% into Oct 28, neither has a verifiable meeting probability, and the thing that would change that is a reachable FedWatch or a contract spanning the meeting. Until then the only directional evidence is a softening consumer on both sides of the border.

fed.stance: On hold at 3.75–4.00%; no verifiable meeting edge
fed.rationale: The Sep 16 FOMC raised the target range 25bp to 3.75–4.00% on a 12–0 vote; that completed action is not itself an October surprise. CME FedWatch returned HTTP 403 on a fresh request, so no single-meeting distribution exists in this snapshot and none is estimated. ZQV26 closed 96.11 on Sep 25, implying a 3.89% October average EFFR — within a basis point of the range midpoint (96.00-96.25 maps to the 3.75-4.00% range), so the contract prices no October move, but its 30-day average is set almost entirely before the Oct 28 decision and it is not a meeting proxy. The dovish consumer evidence is soft: Michigan final sentiment 48.1 beat the 47.6 consensus but is still 3.6 points below August.

boc.stance: On hold at 2.25%; consumer weakness, hawkish column now empty
boc.rationale: The Sep 2 decision held the overnight target at 2.25%, with the next decision Oct 28 alongside the MPR. The only hawkish card previously carried Canada July retail sales on a 'beat' label; that was a sign error and it has been moved to the dovish column — a −0.7% headline contraction (−1.1% in volume) is growth-negative whether or not it beats a −0.8% consensus. With it moved, no BoC hawkish card carries weight, so the Canadian rope reads dovish by absence rather than on positive evidence. CRAU26's quote side implies roughly 2.378% average CORRA against a 2.25% policy rate, but it spans the Oct 28 and Dec 9 decisions and cannot be decomposed into either.

decision_brief.trade_status_rationale: Deliberate abstention, not an absent view. Neither board has a verifiable single-meeting distribution in this snapshot (FedWatch 403 on a fresh request), so there is nothing to express an edge against. The asymmetry worth watching is the Canadian consumer, not the policy rate. This frame is wrong by 2026-10-09, when the October preliminary Michigan prints.
